adverse_media.status: Settled — Revolut signed a settlement with the Bank of Lithuania and took steps to resolve the shortcomings
adverse_media.summary: Lithuania's central bank fined Revolut EUR 3.5m ($3.83m) — the largest fine it has ever issued — after a routine inspection found 'violations and shortcomings in the monitoring of business relationships and operations', leading Revolut not to always properly identify suspicious monetary operations or transactions. The fine was set against the revenues of Revolut Holdings Europe (the group's EU/EEA regulated operations). Revolut said no confirmed instances of money laundering were identified.

adverse_media.status: Reported as under investigation; no public enforcement outcome found as of 2026-10-20
adverse_media.summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority investigated Revolut for allegedly permitting funds to be withdrawn from accounts flagged as suspicious by the National Crime Agency; per the Financial Times, an estimated £1.7m was released from NCA-flagged accounts in July–August 2023, while Revolut said only £500,000 was released.

adverse_media.status: Largely resolved — 2021 accounts filed March 2023 after replacing internal accounting systems; subsequent audit issues and licence delays followed
adverse_media.summary: Auditor BDO LLP flagged it could not satisfy itself on the completeness and occurrence of £477m (~$576m, about three-quarters) of Revolut Ltd's £636m 2021 revenues in long-delayed accounts; the FRC had earlier called Revolut's 2020 audit 'inadequate' with the risk of undetected material misstatement 'unacceptably high'. The warning drew regulatory scrutiny and delayed Revolut's UK banking licence; CFO Mikko Salovaara left in May 2023 and filing of 2022 accounts was delayed a second consecutive year.

adverse_media.status: Ongoing supervisory attention; no enforcement action announced
adverse_media.summary: Lithuania's Financial Crimes Investigation Service (FNTT) told a parliamentary committee that Revolut accounts for ~80% of all suspicious transaction reports sent to Lithuanian officials (about 80,000 of ~100,000 last year), mostly related to potential fraud involving private individuals; Revolut attributed the volume to its scale (57m EEA customers) and AI-driven monitoring.

adverse_media.status: Resolved — filing amended to record UK residence again; earlier entry attributed to an 'administrative error'
adverse_media.summary: The Financial Times reported Revolut had not informed UK regulators in advance of a Companies House filing listing CEO Storonsky as a UAE resident, raising concerns with the FCA, the Bank of England and the Treasury while the company awaited a full UK banking licence.

adverse_media.status: Reported; company attributed measures to EU sanctions compliance
adverse_media.summary: Revolut faced criticism for freezing the accounts of Russian expatriates living in Europe, a measure it said was taken to comply with the latest EU sanctions against Russia.

adverse_media.status: Current — customers migrating to Revolut Bank UK Ltd in phased batches during 2026
adverse_media.summary: Revolut Bank UK Ltd received PRA approval to launch as a fully licensed UK bank after restrictions were lifted following a successful mobilisation period; the new bank serves Revolut's 13m UK customers with FSCS-protected deposits.
adverse_media.category: mitigating — regulatory approval (not adverse, included for completeness of licence status)

output.risk_rationale: Medium. The entity is an active, transparently registered UK company (Companies House 08804411, LEI 213800MQORWPL582SW82, incorporated 6 Dec 2013) with clear ownership: Revolut Group Holdings Ltd (12743269) is the sole PSC holding 75%+ of shares and voting rights since 29 Apr 2022, and no sanctions matches were found for the entity, its owners or its CEO across OFAC SDN, UK OFSI and EU consolidated lists (OpenSanctions aggregate, data current 2026-10-20). No director is a designated PEP, although founder/CEO Nikolay Storonsky carries a PEP-relevant family association (father a senior Gazprom Promgaz executive) that merits standard heightened-review treatment. The medium rating is driven by adverse regulatory history rather than registration or sanctions risk: a record €3.5m Lithuanian central-bank AML fine (Apr 2025, settled), an FCA probe into withdrawals from NCA-flagged accounts (2023, no public outcome), and July 2026 statements that the group generates ~80% of Lithuania's suspicious-transaction reports, plus a governance incident in Dec 2025 when a Companies House filing listed the CEO as UAE-resident without advance notice to regulators (later amended as an administrative error). Offsetting positive: the group received PRA approval in March 2026 to launch Revolut Bank UK Ltd as a fully licensed UK bank after a successful mobilisation period, indicating regulator comfort with its controls.
